title: 8 in 10 Americans Take Health Supplements
paragraphs: In 2025, the global health supplement market was worth almost $210 billion — and around eight in 10 Americans now report taking them.
This is according to a July survey of 3,600 US adults by Pew Research Center.
By far the most common types of supplements being used by Americans are vitamins and minerals like iron and calcium. Two-thirds of respondents said they take these.
Protein supplements — like powders, drinks or bars — are taken by about one-third, and one-quarter said they take omega oil supplements, which are believed to support heart health.
The survey also found that 19% of Americans take herbal supplements like ginseng or ashwagandha, which is commonly used in traditional Indian medicine to manage stress and improve sleep.

The survey also asked if respondents take any other kinds of supplements not included in these categories, and 35% said they do. These "other" supplements include things like probiotics, which may increase good gut bacteria, and melatonin, a hormone that can help with sleep.

Older Americans are the most likely to take supplements — 85% of those aged 65 and older say they take them, compared with 67% of adults under 30. Pew said this could be due to older people being more likely to need help with things like their vitamin D and calcium levels as they age.
However, there is one category of supplement that is used more by younger people — protein.

Among 18-to-29-year-olds, 37% said they take a protein supplement, while 35% of 30-to-49-year-olds said the same. This falls to 29% among those aged 50 to 64, and 23% among respondents who are 65 and over.
This may be in part because younger adults are more influenced by social media, where Pew notes that there are many posts encouraging people to take protein supplements.
